actual_scope: F-star falsifier census: for exact 3-total rational decoders M = sum_j p_j q_j^T on v lines (M_tt nonzero), test the open problem F* of research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas section 7, cert(M) >= floor(2v/3), where cert(M) is maximized over L8 labellings of the largest ordered subset S with K_tt = 1 on S and K_ts = 0 at every incidence M_ts = 0 with t before s. Two exact sides: (A) falsifier hunt via the proven chain cert(M) <= sum_j rank_F2 B[R_j, A_j] over every admissible pairing B (0/1, unit diagonal, ones only where M vanishes); (B) witness side exhibiting a labelling and order with |S| >= floor(2v/3).
scope_change_reason: Pair-collision rule and drawn-card saturation. The OS draw (nonce 298df3754c1488b77620ddda3eb48b27, track adversarial-audit) offered, in order, uniform-transfer-audit, supplier-boundary-audit and selected-stock-envelope. uniform-transfer-audit was completed today on its hosting-implication refinement (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2273, comment https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18939459); supplier-boundary-audit was completed today on its owner-map binding refinement (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2301, comment https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18940382); selected-stock-envelope is covered by a live claim (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18932014) and the PR2084/PR2120 first-stage coefficient work. All three first-choice objects are recent claimed or completed objects, so this session takes the explicit open-problem route instead: open problem F* of the merged research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas package (section 7, OPEN), which the handoffs thread's T=3 open-core request (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18932893 item 4) invites independent eyes on. This keeps the adversarial-audit method of the drawn card (exact counterexample search at a claimed implication) while changing the object to an unclaimed named lemma.
existing_restriction_being_changed: Nothing is relaxed: F* is tested as stated (all exact 3-total rational decoders, all v). Two readings of the quantifier are audited separately: the universal reading (any 0/1 unit-diagonal pairing B with ones only where M vanishes) and the unit-attached reading (B admissible for a concrete root unit, zero on non-orthogonal pairs).
method: Exact stdlib-only arithmetic. Zero patterns of M and of the factor supports drive cert; F2 ranks use Gaussian elimination mod 2. Side A: for each sampled decoder compute the minimum of sum_j rank_F2 B[R_j, A_j] over pairings B (exhaustive for v <= 5, deterministic local search plus B = I baseline for larger v) and compare with floor(2v/3). Side B: search L8 labellings by backtracking and score each by the exact maximum acyclic subset of the incidence digraph (subset DP), then exhibit the maximizing labelling, subset and order as a machine-checked witness. Controls: hand-checkable tiny decoders with brute-force-over-all-labellings cross-check, a deliberately corrupted witness must be rejected, and the proven inequality cert(M) <= sum_j rank_F2 B[R_j, A_j] is rechecked on every instance that has an exhibited witness and a computed pairing cost.
parameter_ranges: v in 4..12; T = 3 totals exactly; factor entries in {-2,-1,0,1,2} with M_tt nonzero on every line; three families: (i) dense random factors, (ii) configuration-style M = P Q^T with P,Q in {-1,0,1}^{v x 3} (many orthogonal pairs, the rank-3 configuration model of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111), (iii) tied-minima 2-adic constructions whose products p_k(t) q_k(t) attain their minimum 2-adic valuation twice or more, the obstruction named in research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas section 7.
nearest_overlapping_prs: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111 (DreamingOfClouds: reductions and certificate limits on tied_min and cex_min_1; records one-copy certificates stopping at 11 and 18, does not search for F* falsifiers and states no F* census); https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2162 and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2277 (char-2 jets CR2/B2 and dense-pairing overcomplete floors; different statements); the source package research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas (merged) states F* as OPEN with about 90 sampled configurations at cert = v. Overlap helper run on refined terms 'cert(M)', 'L8 labelling', '2-adic certificate', 'tied minima', '2v/3' returned only these two predecessors (2026-10-15 05:24 UTC, complete pagination 539 open PRs / 1038 discussions).
optimistic_full_cost_budget: No kappa, supplier, word or moment budget is in play; this is a missing-lemma audit. The whole-construction price is the exact census itself: all counts, ranks and witnesses are recomputed by the verifier in one bounded run (no sampling left implicit).
bottleneck_link: F-star is the named route to closing every open T = 3 window at once (research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas section 7 consequence, PROVEN given F*): it would give cost >= floor(2v/3) >= N(h) for all open T = 3 windows. A falsifier would redirect the T = 3 decoder route; certified evidence widens the domain where the closure argument can be trusted. Finite supplier improvements matter only under the retained transfer obligations, and this audit addresses one such inherited implication without touching kappa.
stop_rule: Stop at the first exact falsifier (an instance with min_B sum_j rank_F2 B[R_j, A_j] < floor(2v/3), fully recorded), or, absent one, at the declared-domain census with machine-checked witnesses for every sampled instance and the exact obstruction recorded for any instance where no witness reaches the threshold. Time cap: about 40 minutes of computation, one bounded pivot maximum.
success_evidence: A falsifier instance with exact pairing-cost minimization and the failing threshold recorded, or a scoped census: exact counts per family and v, the minimum achieved witness ratio |S|/v, every witness replayed by verify.py, the proven-chain inequality checked per instance, and the tiny-domain brute-force cross-check agreeing with the search engine.
falsification_test: Side A is itself the falsifier test for F*; its negative control is a constructed instance where the pairing cost is forced below threshold by hand (if such exists in the domain). Side B witnesses are rejected if any K_tt = 1 or any before-pair constraint fails; a corrupted copy of a stored witness must fail verification.
time_compute_cap: One session; compute capped at about 40 minutes single-process stdlib Python; no SAT solver, no third-party packages, no large downloads.
predecessor_authors: F* and the cert(M) definition: the research/root-unit-decoder-lemmas package (merged, Douglas Colkitt with OpenAI Codex assistance lineage; Lemmas A and B and the L8 lemma are its PROVEN results). Rank-3 configuration model, tied_min and cex_min_1 examples and certificate limits: DreamingOfClouds, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2111 and https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2162. Independent CR2/B2 audit: Aaron Wang, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2293. This package does not claim their results; it adds a declared-domain F* falsifier census and machine-checked witnesses.

Controls pass: three tiny-domain brute-force cross-checks agree with the search engine exactly, corrupted and wrong-order witnesses are rejected, the diagonal control gives cert = 3, and the proven chain cert(M) <= cost(B) is rechecked per instance. Recorded in CERTIFICATE.json (census digest 3237519deb9ec377f5a8a86b7b4b1e8197074ee8d0dd0e653cfcea1104c9e6e8) and CENSUS-RECORDS.json. This is evidence for F*, not a proof: witnesses are lower bounds on cert(M), and only the recorded instances are covered.

open_questions.why_it_matters: F-star would close every open T = 3 window; the tied-minima family is the only obstruction the source package could not order.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the census family (iii) to v = 13..18 with the same witness engine and record the minimum achieved |S|/v as a function of the tied-minima count.

open_questions.question: Is the universal reading of F-star (any 0/1 unit-diagonal pairing with ones only where M vanishes) equivalent to the unit-attached reading (B admissible for a concrete root unit)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A falsifier for the universal reading would refute the lemma as stated in section 7; a separation would pin which reading the window-closure consequence needs.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate small units (A3, A4, D4) with their orthogonality patterns and compare min_B pairing costs inside and outside the admissible family on the same decoders.
open_questions.blocked_by: Needs the unit Gram tables wired into the search; the current census keeps the two readings separate by construction.
